nodes.description: Breathing disturbances arise from MeCP2-dependent dysfunction in respiratory control networks, including ventrolateral medulla and pontine circuits. Within the pons the lesion has been localised to the Koelliker-Fuse area, which drives post-inspiration and can reset the respiratory oscillator: Mecp2 heterozygous mice lose GABAergic perisomatic boutons there, and the link is bidirectional, since boosting local GABA reuptake blockade reduces breathing irregularity in mutant mice while blocking GABA-A receptors in the same area of healthy rats reproduces the Rett respiratory phenotype.

nodes.description: Cortical circuits in Rett syndrome sit shifted toward excitation, and the shift is measurable in patients rather than only inferred from models. Paired-pulse transcranial magnetic stimulation of primary motor cortex in typical Rett patients shows a raised excitation index, driven by reduced short-interval intracortical inhibition and increased intracortical facilitation, which the investigators read as GABAergic dysfunction. Long-interval intracortical inhibition is likewise reduced, and LTP-like plasticity is abolished and scales with motor disability. The GABAergic attribution is the study authors' interpretation of the neurophysiology, not a direct measurement of interneuron function in these patients.

nodes.description: MeCP2 normally binds methylated CpG dinucleotides and participates in transcriptional repression and activation. Loss or altered dosage of MeCP2 changes neuronal gene-expression programs, providing the proximal molecular bridge from MECP2 mutation to downstream neurodevelopmental defects. The regulatory function lost here is broader than gene-specific repression. MeCP2 is present in neuronal nuclei at near histone-octamer abundance, so its removal changes chromatin state globally rather than at a defined target set; most of its protein partners are mRNA splicing factors, and it also loads the Super Elongation Complex scaffold AFF4 onto synaptic-plasticity genes. Chromatin architecture, alternative splicing, and transcription elongation are therefore all disrupted alongside transcriptional output.

nodes.description: MeCP2 loss is not confined to neurons, and MeCP2-deficient glia actively injure neighbouring neurons rather than merely failing to support them. Conditioned medium from Mecp2-null microglia carries a fivefold excess of glutamate that stunts and beads dendrites and damages postsynaptic glutamatergic components within a day, an effect abolished by blocking microglial glutamate synthesis or release or by antagonising neuronal glutamate receptors. Oligodendrocyte lineage cells contribute separately: deleting MeCP2 from them alone produces hindlimb clasping, and restoring it to them alone in otherwise null mice improves locomotion and clasping. Both results are from mouse systems and the corresponding experiment cannot be done in human brain, so this node is model-derived.
